resource_limits.scope: each proxy container (EQProxy and HAProxy); origin, sink and generator are outside

generator.what: golang.org/x/net/http2 client over TLS (ALPN h2), real certificate verification, StrictMaxConcurrentStreams so one transport is one connection, closed-loop, no coordinated-omission correction

disclosure.topology: one Linux host; origin, sink, both proxies and the generator are containers on one bridge network; no host port publishing on the measured path
equivalence: same HTTP/1.1 origin (path-addressed body, Content-Length, keep-alive)
same certificate, TLS 1.3, ALPN h2, 30 s idle timeout
same container port 19443, maxconn 20000 in both
no compression enabled in either product; no rules/rewrites in this scenario
100 client streams per connection (plan §3); EQProxy advertises 128, HAProxy's default tune.h2.max-concurrent-streams is 100
differences: EQProxy translates every h2 stream into one HTTP/1.1 exchange through its engine (ADR-0006); HAProxy forwards natively over HTX

load_c4s100_1k.note: Local HTTP/2 sink (same binary, real TLS + h2) measures the client+sink pair; the slower of the two is the ceiling, so this is a lower bound on what the generator can push.

load_c4s8_1m.note: Local HTTP/2 sink (same binary, real TLS + h2) measures the client+sink pair; the slower of the two is the ceiling, so this is a lower bound on what the generator can push.

gaps.note: metric ratios > 1 favour EQProxy; latency ratios > 1 mean EQProxy had the lower end-to-end latency; cpu ratio > 1 means EQProxy spent more CPU per second for the same offered load.
